cards.text: This is the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1). Just before this, he said the work done under the sun was grievous to him, and that everything is futile, a pursuit of the wind (Ecclesiastes 2:17). Now he starts a new thought about seasons and time, and friend, he is thinking BIG.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says only some parts of life get their own season.

cards.text: Then he starts his list of times, and he opens with the two biggest moments in any life.

cards.question: The Teacher opens his list with the two biggest moments in any life. What pair of times is that?

answers.text: A time to be born and a time to die
A time to wake and a time to sleep
A time to come and a time to go

cards.text: Next comes a time to plant and a time to uproot, a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build.

cards.question: Born and die, plant and uproot, break down and build: so far, every time in the Teacher's list comes paired with its ___.

cards.text: Then it gets personal: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance. Dancing on a gold base is mostly hopping, friend, but believe me, I GO for it.

cards.question: Weeping and laughing, mourning and dancing. What is the Teacher pairing in this part of his list?

cards.text: Then there's a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, and a time to embrace. With a mustache this big, friend, I hug people by ACCIDENT just turning around.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says there's also a time to hold back from embracing.

cards.text: Next comes a time to search and a time to count as lost. Then a time to keep, and friend, the junk drawer I spent years in only EVER heard that word.

cards.question: Following his pattern, what does the Teacher pair with a time to keep?

cards.text: Then a time to tear and a time to mend. Then a time to be silent, and friend, I am LOUD, so I am still working on that one.

cards.question: The Teacher pairs a time to be silent with a time to ___.

cards.text: His last line opens with a time to love and a time to hate. Then comes a time for war.

cards.question: War is the last time in the Teacher's list. Following his pattern, what is it paired with?

cards.text: After that whole list, the Teacher asks one question: "What does the worker gain from his toil?" Friend, that's the same question everybody hitting snooze on a Monday morning is asking.
Then he says he has seen the burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them. Friend, I KNOW occupied: one stamper, a whole lot of cookie boxes, and ovens that never take a day off.
Then he says something about everything God has made. Friend, after a question that heavy, I am leaning in REAL close for this one.

cards.question: In its time, what does the Teacher say God has made everything?

cards.text: Then he goes deeper: God has also set eternity in the hearts of men. A heart living by the calendar, and God puts FOREVER inside it.

cards.question: God has set eternity in people's hearts. True or false: the Teacher says people can fathom all of God's work from beginning to end.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says he knows what's best for people while they live. Friend, I have waited my WHOLE stamper life for somebody to just tell me.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say there's nothing better for people to do while they live?

cards.text: He adds that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with NO labor at all, and trust me, the work is the good part.

cards.question: Eating, drinking and finding satisfaction in all your labor? The Teacher calls that the ___ of God.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says he knows something about everything God does. Friend, the only thing I know for sure is that sprinkles get EVERYWHERE.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say about everything God does?
Everything God does endures forever. True or false: the Teacher says nothing can be taken from it.
God's work lasts forever, and nothing can be added to it or taken from it. Why does the Teacher say God does it that way?

answers.text: So that people would fear Him
So that people would rest from work
So that kings would rule wisely

cards.text: He ends with this: what exists has already been, and what will be has already been. Kind of like my jokes, friend: even the NEW ones have already been told.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says God will call to account what has passed.
